title: Getting Things Done
description: Describe services and report information formally using the passive in all tenses and with modals, the causative have/get something done, and passive reporting structures (it is said that..., he is believed to...). Vocabulary: services, media, crime and justice.
objectives: Use the passive voice in all tenses and with modal verbs
Use have/get something done to talk about services
Report information formally with it is said that... and subject + is said to...
Understand and use vocabulary for crime, justice and news reporting

lessons.title: The Passive in All Tenses
lessons.summary: Membentuk dan menggunakan kalimat pasif dalam semua tenses.
objectives: Form the passive in present, past, perfect and future tenses
Decide when to use the passive and when to include the agent (by...)
Avoid common errors with past participles and continuous passives
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Why use the passive?
We use the passive when the **action** or the **receiver** of the action is more important than the person who does it, when the doer is unknown or obvious, or in formal and scientific writing.
- *My bike **has been stolen**.* (We don't know who did it.)
- *The suspect **was arrested** last night.* (Obviously by the police.)

### Form: be + past participle
Only the verb **be** changes tense; the main verb is always a **past participle**.

| Tense | Active | Passive |
| --- | --- | --- |
| present simple | They **clean** the rooms daily. | The rooms **are cleaned** daily. |
| present continuous | They **are painting** the hall. | The hall **is being painted**. |
| past simple | They **built** it in 1925. | It **was built** in 1925. |
| past continuous | They **were questioning** him. | He **was being questioned**. |
| present perfect | They **have sold** the house. | The house **has been sold**. |
| past perfect | They **had cancelled** the flight. | The flight **had been cancelled**. |
| future (will) | They **will announce** the results. | The results **will be announced**. |
| be going to | They**'re going to** close the road. | The road **is going to be closed**. |

### The agent: by + ...
Include *by + agent* only when it adds important information:
- ✓ *The novel was written **by a 17-year-old student**.* (surprising, important)
- ✗ *The thief was arrested by the police.* (obvious — omit *by the police*)

### Which verbs can be passive?
Only **transitive** verbs (verbs with an object). *Happen, arrive, die, seem* cannot be passive:
- ✗ *The accident was happened at night.* → ✓ *The accident happened at night.*

### Questions and negatives
- ***Has** the parcel **been delivered** yet?*
- *The meeting **wasn't recorded**.*
- *When **was** the bridge **built**?*

> **Catatan:** Bahasa Indonesia memakai awalan **di-** (*dibangun, dicuri*), sedangkan bahasa Inggris memakai **be + V3** dan *be* harus sesuai tense: *sedang dicat* = *is being painted*; *sudah dijual* = *has been sold*. Jangan lupa bentuk V3 yang tidak beraturan: *stolen, written, built, chosen*.

grammar.pattern: subject + be (any tense) + past participle (+ by agent)
grammar.example: The film was directed by a young woman.

mistakes.why: The passive needs the past participle (written), not the past simple.

mistakes.wrong: The accident was happened at midnight.
mistakes.why: Happen is intransitive (no object), so it cannot be passive.

mistakes.right: The house is being painted at the moment.
mistakes.why: The continuous passive is be + being + past participle.

sections.summary: Passive = **be + past participle**; only *be* changes for tense (*is done, is being done, was done, has been done, had been done, will be done*). Use it when the action or receiver matters more than the doer, and add *by + agent* only when it is important. *Ringkasan: di- dalam bahasa Indonesia = be + V3 dalam bahasa Inggris.*

reviewCards.back: Only when the doer is important or surprising.

questions.explanation: *At the moment* → an action in progress → present continuous passive: **is being renovated**.

questions.explanation: Present perfect active (*has stolen*) → present perfect passive (**has been stolen**). *Someone* is unknown, so we omit the agent.

questions.explanation: The past perfect passive is **had been + past participle**: *had already been stolen* (steal – stole – stolen).

lessons.title: Passive with Modals and Infinitives
lessons.summary: Kalimat pasif dengan modal (must be done) serta infinitive dan gerund pasif (to be done, being done).
objectives: Use modal + be + past participle (must be done, can be found)
Use passive infinitives (needs to be signed) and passive gerunds (being told)
Write rules and instructions in a formal passive style
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Modal + be + past participle
After a modal verb, the passive is always **be + past participle**.

| Modal | Example | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| can / can't | Tickets **can be bought** online. | possibility |
| must | All bags **must be checked**. | obligation |
| should | Plants **should be watered** twice a week. | advice |
| might / may | The match **might be cancelled**. | possibility |
| will | The road **will be closed** tomorrow. | future |
| have to | The form **has to be signed**. | obligation |

Passive with modals is very common in **rules, notices and instructions**:
- *Phones **must be switched off** during the exam.*
- *This medicine **shouldn't be taken** on an empty stomach.*

### Passive infinitive: to be + past participle
Use it after verbs and adjectives that take *to*:
- *The report **needs to be finished** by Monday.*
- *I **expect to be told** the results soon.*
- *She **wants to be promoted**.*
- *This task is **easy to be done*** ✗ → *This task is easy to do* ✓ (after *easy, hard, difficult*, use the active infinitive).

### Passive gerund: being + past participle
Use it after verbs and prepositions that take *-ing*:
- *I hate **being told** what to do.*
- *He **avoided being seen**.*
- *She's afraid of **being criticised**.*

### need + -ing (British English)
*The car **needs washing*** = *The car **needs to be washed***. Both are passive in meaning.

### Common errors
| Wrong | Right |
| --- | --- |
| must be finish | must **be finished** |
| can found | can **be found** |
| hate to told | hate **being told** / hate **to be told** |

> **Catatan:** Setelah modal (*can, must, should, might*), pasif selalu **be + V3**: *harus diisi* = *must be filled in*; *bisa ditemukan* = *can be found*. Untuk *suka/benci diperlakukan...*, pakai **being + V3**: *Saya tidak suka disuruh-suruh* = *I don't like being told what to do.*

mistakes.why: After modal + be, use the past participle.

sections.summary: Passive with modals: **modal + be + past participle** (*must be done, can be found*). Passive infinitive: **to be + past participle** (*needs to be signed*). Passive gerund: **being + past participle** (*hate being told*). These forms are typical of rules, notices and formal instructions. *Ringkasan: setelah modal selalu be + V3.*

questions.prompt: Complete the rule with ONE word.
questions.text: All phones must ___ switched off during the exam.
questions.explanation: Passive with a modal: **must be + past participle** → *must be switched off*.

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the passive.
questions.sentence: You should water these plants twice a week.
answers: These plants should be watered twice a week.
questions.explanation: *should + verb* → **should be + past participle**: *These plants should be watered twice a week.*

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option.
questions.context: I'm an adult. I really hate ___ what to do by my older brother.
questions.explanation: The speaker receives the action, so we need a passive form after *hate*: **being told** (passive gerund). *Telling* and *to tell* are active; *be told* cannot follow *hate*.

questions.prompt: Complete the school notice with words from the bank.
questions.text: The trip form can be ___ from the school website. It needs to be ___ by a parent, and it must be ___ to the school office by Friday.
questions.explanation: After *can be / needs to be / must be* we need past participles: **downloaded, signed, returned**. *Signing* and *return* are not past participles.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option for this medicine label.
questions.text: This medicine ___ taken on an empty stomach.
questions.explanation: The medicine receives the action → modal passive: **shouldn't be taken**.

questions.prompt: Find the error.
questions.explanation: Future passive: **will be + past participle** → *will be introduced*.

lessons.title: Causative: Have/Get Something Done
lessons.summary: Menggunakan have/get something done untuk layanan yang dikerjakan orang lain, serta have someone do / get someone to do.
objectives: Use have/get + object + past participle for services
Use have something done for unpleasant experiences (I had my phone stolen)
Use have someone do and get someone to do something
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Services: someone else does the job
Compare:
- *I **cut** my hair.* → I did it myself.
- *I **had** my hair **cut**.* → A hairdresser did it for me.

### Form: have/get + object + past participle
| Tense | Example |
| --- | --- |
| present simple | I **have** my car **serviced** every year. |
| present continuous | We**'re having** the kitchen **redecorated**. |
| past simple | She **got** her phone screen **replaced**. |
| present perfect | Have you **had** your eyes **tested** recently? |
| future | I**'ll get** the documents **translated**. |
| modal | You should **have** that tooth **checked**. |

⚠️ Word order matters: **have + object + past participle**.
- ✓ *I had the house painted.* (someone painted it for me)
- ✗ *I had painted the house.* (= past perfect: I painted it myself, earlier)

*Get* is slightly more informal than *have*, and can suggest effort: *I finally **got** the printer **fixed**.*

### Unpleasant experiences
The same structure describes something bad that **happened to** you (no arrangement!):
- *Ana **had her car stolen** last week.*
- *He **had his nose broken** in a football match.*

### Making someone do something
| Structure | Meaning | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| have + person + infinitive (no to) | ask/arrange (often in a work context) | I'll **have my assistant call** you. |
| get + person + to-infinitive | persuade | I **got my brother to help** me move. |

### Quick comparison
| Sentence | Who did the action? |
| --- | --- |
| I fixed the bike. | me |
| I had/got the bike fixed. | a mechanic (a service) |
| I got my dad to fix the bike. | my dad (I persuaded him) |

> **Catatan:** Bahasa Indonesia sering memakai kata kerja aktif untuk layanan: *Saya potong rambut kemarin* — padahal tukang cukur yang memotong. Dalam bahasa Inggris gunakan **I had my hair cut** (bukan *I cut my hair*, kecuali Anda memotongnya sendiri).

examples.en: I've just had my hair cut at a salon near the station.
examples.id: Saya baru saja potong rambut di salon dekat stasiun.

mistakes.wrong: I cut my hair at the hairdresser's yesterday.
mistakes.right: I had my hair cut at the hairdresser's yesterday.
mistakes.why: When a professional does it, use the causative have/get + object + past participle.

mistakes.right: We had the house painted by a local company.
mistakes.why: The object comes between have and the past participle.

mistakes.wrong: I got my brother help me.
mistakes.right: I got my brother to help me.

sections.summary: Use **have/get + object + past participle** when someone else does a job for you (*I had my car serviced*) or when something bad happens to you (*I had my phone stolen*). Use **have + person + infinitive** and **get + person + to-infinitive** to talk about making or persuading someone to do something. *Ringkasan: perhatikan urutan: have + benda + V3.*

lessons.title: It Is Said That... / He Is Said To...
lessons.summary: Melaporkan informasi secara formal dengan pasif dan kata kerja pelaporan (say, believe, think, report).
objectives: Use It + passive reporting verb + that-clause
Use subject + passive reporting verb + to-infinitive (present and past)
Recognise this distancing style in news reports
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### Why journalists use it
News reports often contain information that is not 100% confirmed or whose source is general (*people, experts, the police*). Passive reporting structures let the writer **report without taking responsibility**.

Common verbs: *say, believe, think, report, know, expect, consider, estimate, allege, understand*.

### Pattern 1: It + passive verb + that-clause
| Active | Passive |
| --- | --- |
| People say that the house is haunted. | **It is said that** the house is haunted. |
| Experts believe that prices will rise. | **It is believed that** prices will rise. |
| They reported that two people were injured. | **It was reported that** two people were injured. |

### Pattern 2: Subject + passive verb + to-infinitive
The subject of the that-clause becomes the subject of the sentence. The infinitive form depends on **time**:

| Time of the action | Infinitive | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| same time / general | **to + verb** | The house **is said to be** haunted. |
| in progress now | **to be + -ing** | The minister **is thought to be hiding** something. |
| earlier (past) | **to have + past participle** | The thieves **are believed to have escaped** through the window. |
| future (with expect) | **to + verb** | Prices **are expected to rise**. |

### How to transform
*People believe that the thieves escaped through the window.*
1. Subject of the that-clause → *The thieves*
2. Passive reporting verb → *are believed*
3. The escape happened before the believing → **to have escaped**
→ ***The thieves are believed to have escaped through the window.***

### Passive actions inside the infinitive
*The painting **is thought to have been stolen** in 1990.* (to have been + past participle)

### Watch out
- ✗ *It is said the house to be haunted.* — don't mix the patterns.
- ✗ *He is said to escaping.* — use the infinitive.

> **Catatan:** Struktur ini setara dengan *konon*, *diyakini*, *dilaporkan*, *diperkirakan* dalam berita: *Diperkirakan dua ribu orang hadir* → *It is estimated that two thousand people attended.* Jika aksi terjadi lebih dulu dari pelaporan, gunakan **to have + V3**.

examples.en: It is believed that the castle was built in the 12th century.
examples.id: Diyakini bahwa kastil itu dibangun pada abad ke-12.

examples.en: The castle is believed to have been built in the 12th century.
examples.id: Kastil itu diyakini dibangun pada abad ke-12.
examples.note: Pattern 2 with a past passive infinitive.

examples.en: The suspect is thought to be hiding in the mountains.
examples.id: Tersangka diduga sedang bersembunyi di pegunungan.

examples.en: The new stadium is expected to open in 2028.
examples.id: Stadion baru itu diperkirakan dibuka pada tahun 2028.

vocabulary.example: The man allegedly stole the documents.
It is estimated that 5,000 people attended.
The old hotel is said to be haunted.
The source of the report is unclear.
The police have not confirmed the report.

grammar.example: It is reported that the president is ill.

grammar.pattern: subject + is/are + said/believed + to + verb / to be + -ing
grammar.example: She is said to be very rich.

grammar.pattern: subject + is/are + said/believed + to have + past participle
grammar.example: He is believed to have left the country.

mistakes.wrong: The thieves are believed to escape last night.
mistakes.right: The thieves are believed to have escaped last night.
mistakes.why: The escape happened before the belief, so use to have + past participle.

mistakes.wrong: It is said the house to be haunted.
mistakes.right: The house is said to be haunted.
mistakes.why: Don't mix the patterns: use either It is said that... or Subject + is said to...

mistakes.wrong: The singer is reported earning millions.
mistakes.right: The singer is reported to earn millions.
mistakes.why: After a passive reporting verb, use the to-infinitive.

sections.summary: Report information formally with **It is said/believed/reported that + clause** or **Subject + is said/believed + to-infinitive**. Use *to + verb* for present states, *to be + -ing* for actions in progress and *to have + past participle* for earlier actions. *Ringkasan: struktur ini = konon / diyakini / dilaporkan dalam bahasa berita.*

reviewCards.front: He is believed to have left.
reviewCards.back: Dia diyakini sudah pergi (earlier action → to have + V3).

reviewCards.front: She is thought to be hiding.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form.
questions.instructions: Hint: It + be + past participle + that...
questions.text: It ___ that the castle was built in the 12th century.
questions.explanation: The impersonal passive pattern is **It is believed that...** (diyakini bahwa...).

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it means the same.
questions.sentence: People say that the old house on Kenari Street is haunted.
questions.cue: Begin with: The old house on Kenari Street ...
answers: The old house on Kenari Street is said to be haunted.
questions.explanation: Subject + **is said to + verb** (same time): *The old house on Kenari Street is said to be haunted.*

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence so that it means the same.
questions.sentence: People believe that the thieves escaped through the bathroom window.
answers: The thieves are believed to have escaped through the bathroom window.
questions.explanation: The escape happened before the believing → **to have + past participle**: *are believed to have escaped*.

questions.prompt: Complete the news sentence with the correct infinitive form of the verb in brackets.
questions.text: The company's director is reported ___ (resign) last week.
questions.explanation: *Last week* shows an earlier action → **to have resigned**.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'People think that the minister is hiding something at the moment'?
options: The minister is thought to be hiding something.
The minister is thought to have hidden something.
The minister thinks he is hiding something.
It thinks that the minister hides something.
questions.explanation: An action in progress now → **to be + -ing**: *The minister is thought to be hiding something.* Option 2 refers to an earlier action.

questions.prompt: Find the error.
questions.explanation: After a passive reporting verb, use the infinitive. The escape was earlier (*last night*), so: **to have escaped**.

lessons.title: Vocabulary: Crime, Justice and the News
lessons.summary: Kosakata tentang kejahatan, hukum, dan berita, digabung dengan kalimat pasif khas laporan berita.
objectives: Use vocabulary for the stages of a criminal case (arrest, charge, trial, verdict, sentence)
Use the correct prepositions (arrested for, charged with, accused of, sentenced to)
Understand and write short news reports in a passive style
lessons.completionCriteria: Read all sections and score at least 70% on the mini quiz. (Baca semua bagian dan raih skor minimal 70% pada mini quiz.)

sections.explanation:
### From crime to sentence
| Stage | Vocabulary | Example (often passive!) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. The crime | burglary, robbery, fraud, shoplifting | A shop **was robbed** on Main Street. |
| 2. Investigation | witness, evidence, suspect | A **suspect** is being questioned. |
| 3. Arrest | arrest sb **for** sth | A man **was arrested for** burglary. |
| 4. Charge | charge sb **with** sth | He **was charged with** fraud. |
| 5. Trial | stand trial, court, jury, judge | She will **stand trial** in May. |
| 6. Verdict | guilty / not guilty, convict, acquit | He **was found guilty**. |
| 7. Sentence | sentence sb **to** ..., fine | She **was sentenced to** three years. |

### Prepositions to remember
| Verb | Preposition | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| arrest | for | arrested **for** theft |
| charge | with | charged **with** theft |
| accuse | of | accused **of** theft |
| convict | of | convicted **of** theft |
| sentence | to | sentenced **to** five years |
| fine | (amount) for | fined $500 **for** speeding |

### The language of news reports
News writers often use the passive and distancing language because:
- the victim or event matters more than the criminal;
- the facts are not yet proven.

| Feature | Example |
| --- | --- |
| passive | *Three people **have been injured** in an attack.* |
| reporting passive | *The man **is believed to have entered** through a window.* |
| allegedly / reportedly | *He **allegedly** stole €2 million.* |
| present perfect for news | *A 34-year-old man **has been arrested**.* |

### Media vocabulary
*headline* (title of a news story), *coverage* (how much the media reports something), *press conference*, *eyewitness account*, *breaking news*.

### Services connection
Some crime vocabulary is connected to services: you can **have your locks changed** after a burglary, or **get a document certified** by a lawyer.

> **Catatan:** Perhatikan preposisi yang berbeda: *arrested **for***, *charged **with***, *accused **of***, *sentenced **to***. *Suspect* = tersangka; *witness* = saksi; *verdict* = putusan; *sentence* = hukuman/vonis (juga berarti 'kalimat' dalam konteks bahasa).

examples.en: A 34-year-old man has been arrested in connection with the robbery.

grammar.pattern: be arrested for / charged with / accused of + noun or -ing
grammar.example: She was accused of lying to the court.
He was sentenced to 200 hours of community service.

grammar.note: Present perfect passive for new information.

mistakes.why: Charge takes with; accuse and convict take of.

mistakes.right: The police found a lot of evidence.

mistakes.right: She was sentenced to five years.
mistakes.why: The preposition after sentence is to.

sections.summary: A criminal case moves from **crime → investigation → arrest → charge → trial → verdict → sentence**. Learn the prepositions: *arrested for, charged with, accused/convicted of, sentenced to, fined for*. News reports use the passive, the present perfect and distancing words such as *allegedly*. *Ringkasan: perhatikan preposisi dan bentuk pasif dalam berita.*

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word.
questions.instructions: Hint: this person saw what happened.
questions.context: A ___ told the police that she had seen two men running away from the shop.
questions.explanation: A **witness** (saksi) is someone who saw an event. A *suspect* is a person believed to have committed the crime; a *judge* and a *jury* decide the case in court.

questions.prompt: Match each word with its definition.

pairs.right: a person the police think may have committed a crime
the decision of a court: guilty or not guilty
the punishment given by a judge
the process of examining a case in court

questions.explanation: These words describe different stages of a criminal case. Note that *sentence* also means *kalimat* in grammar.

questions.prompt: Put the fragments in order to make the first sentence of a news report.
fragments: which took place on Friday night.
questions.explanation: A typical news opening: subject → present perfect passive (**has been arrested**) → *in connection with* + event → extra information.

questions.prompt: Complete the news report with words from the bank.
questions.text: The man was ___ with burglary and will stand ___ next month. If he is found guilty, he could be ___ to five years in prison.
questions.explanation: **charged with** (didakwa), **stand trial** (diadili), **sentenced to** (dijatuhi hukuman). *Accused* takes *of*, not *with*.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct prepositions.
questions.text: The teenager was arrested ___ shoplifting and later charged ___ theft.
questions.explanation: **arrested for** + crime; **charged with** + crime.

questions.prompt: Which word in a news report shows that a crime has NOT been proved yet?
questions.explanation: **Allegedly** (konon/diduga) shows that something is claimed but not proved. *Guilty* and *convicted* mean it has been proved in court.

unitTestQuestions.context: When the inspectors finally arrived, the documents ___.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: The destruction happened before a past moment, and the documents received the action → past perfect passive: **had been destroyed**.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence in the passive.
unitTestQuestions.sentence: They are going to announce the winners on Friday.
answers: The winners are going to be announced on Friday.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *be going to + verb* → **be going to be + past participle**.

unitTestQuestions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the causative. Use the verb in brackets.
unitTestQuestions.text: My laptop wasn't working, so I ___ it ___ (repair) at a shop near the station.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: Someone at the shop repaired it → **had/got + object + past participle**: *I had it repaired.*
The theft happened earlier (*last year*) and the painting received the action → past passive infinitive: **to have been stolen**.

answers: The bridge is currently being repaired.
The bridge is currently being fixed.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: *Sedang di-...* = present continuous passive: **is being + past participle** → *The bridge is being repaired.*

options: Thanks, I had it cut yesterday.
Thanks, I cut it by a hairdresser yesterday.
Thanks, I had cut it yesterday.
Thanks, I have it cut yesterday.
unitTestQuestions.explanation: A hairdresser did it → causative past simple: **I had it cut yesterday.** *I had cut it* is the past perfect (I cut it myself), and *have* doesn't match *yesterday*.
